semantics.start: agent is inside p_1 at t_0 (Alg. 3 line 1/17; p. 400 'agent x starts in A')
semantics.rooms: entering any room of C_p is a visit and must be the next story element (STAR §2.1; p. 400 'C in G22 not directly reachable ... passing only vertices from sensors'; p. 401 'C in G3 must pass A to reach B, this subproblem dies')
semantics.c_p: C_p is not pinned down for stories that omit a map room. The paper defines C_p as the set of distinct elements of p (§2.1) and treats only rooms in the story as obstacles (Fig. 2 caption). Read that way, story (C,B) would make A free space: A would stop being a vertex and R1 and R2 would merge through it. This fixture keeps the map's rooms A, B, C as C_p. Every case was re-checked under both readings (C_p = map rooms; C_p = story rooms with other rooms as free space) by explicit walk enumeration, and no expected 'consistent' value changes.
semantics.end: agent is inside p_n at t_f (Alg. 3 line 21 requires the copy of p_n in G_{m+1})
semantics.single: every recording is made by x; x is inside o for the whole activation-deactivation interval
semantics.multi: occupancy events only change connectivity; x may cross a beam only at a recorded event of that beam; x may be inside o only while o is active
semantics.initial_sensor_state: all occupancy sensors inactive at t_0 (implicit in the paper)

maps.verified_by: Read off a 600-dpi render of p. 394: doorways a (left) and b (top, left of the beam) open into the same free component L; c opens into Rt, which also contains the space right of the beam and the unlabelled right room. cases.verified_by: Brute force over the region-level model of Fig. 2 (independent time-expanded search, not shipped, state = (location, story index, entry label); the shipped equivalent is tests/oracles/brute.py) gives inconsistent under both end conventions; the copies of the room at which visit i can happen (entry label -> Fig. 4 name) are exactly G1/G21/G3 for p2=C and G4/G5 for p3=B and none for p4=A, matching the paper's narrative. Independently, Algorithms 1-2 recomputed every Fig. 4 subgraph exactly (with G3's unreachable goal b2r dropped), Fig. 5's directed arcs reproduced exactly, and a DP over the chained graph (Alg. 3 with r_i -> r_j fixed) gives the same subproblems and false. Agrees with the paper.

fig6b_G0_4_after_cliquification.difference: Algorithm 4 also adds b2l-b2r (both become neighbours of o2 after o1 is removed): K5. The figure omits it. An edge between two goal vertices is never usable (goals are terminal), so the omission does not change any answer.

cases.verified_by: Brute force over the region-level model (independent search, not shipped; shipped equivalent tests/oracles/brute.py; multi semantics: occupancy events only toggle passability, x may cross a beam only at a recorded event of that beam, at most once per event) finds the witness above; consistent under both end conventions. Fig. 6(a) recomputed exactly by Algorithm 2 with V_C = C_p U {o1,o2} U {A}; Fig. 6(b) by Algorithm 4 (differs from the drawing only by the useless goal-goal edge b2l-b2r). The 9 Fig. 7 subgraphs were computed with Algorithm 4, their starts/goals and the 10 dashed crossing arcs transcribed from a 500-dpi render of p. 404, and a DP over this chained graph returns consistent. Agrees with the paper.
